lore_summary.en: A herdsman's ambition, a court astrologer's prophecy, and a dynasty is born. Ardeshir refounds Pars.
lore_summary.fa: اردشیر پس از کشتن اردوان، ایران پراکنده را با جنگ‌های پی‌درپی متحد کرد. داستان کرم هفتواد نشان می‌دهد که او نه تنها دشمنان نظامی بلکه قدرت‌های محلی جادویی را هم از بین برد. با تأسیس تیسفون و احیای آتشکده‌های زرتشتی، ایران ساسانی را بنیان گذاشت.

scenes.body_en: Ardeshir did not stop at killing Ardavan. He kept moving, and the thing he was building became clear only after several years of constant war: he was not merely replacing one king with another. He was replacing a system. The Ashkanian model had been loose — regional lords kept their thrones, paid tribute, sent soldiers when asked, and otherwise ran their own affairs. Ardeshir ended that. He marched against each regional king in turn, absorbed their territories, and installed governors who answered to him. Iran was being pulled back into a single shape.

The Shahnameh gives this consolidation a story it deserves: Haftvad and the worm. A girl who spun thread had found a small worm in an apple and kept it in her spindle case. Wherever the worm went, her thread grew fine and abundant. Her father Haftvad grew rich, then powerful, then a king in his own right, ruling a fortress on the edge of Ardeshir's new empire. The worm had grown with the fortune — it was now enormous, kept in the fortress and fed on milk and flour. It was the source of everything Haftvad had, and Haftvad knew it.

Ardeshir attacked Haftvad twice and failed. The worm's luck held against armies. He won on the third attempt through cunning: he sent a trusted man disguised as a merchant carrying sesame and honey, with molten lead hidden in the cargo. The merchant gained access to the worm's chamber under the pretense of feeding it, and poured the metal down its throat. The worm died. Haftvad's fortress fell the next morning, its defenders suddenly bereft of whatever had been sustaining them.

This is the Shahnameh's way of saying that Ardeshir's consolidation was not merely military. He was also ending the old local sorceries, the regional loyalties that outlasted every dynasty, the stubborn particular powers that made Iran ungovernable as a whole. The worm was all of those things at once. When it died, centralized Iran became possible. Ardeshir built his capital at Ctesiphon, restored the Zoroastrian fire temples, and reigned long enough to hand his son a functioning empire.

battle.intro_en: A court astrologer read the stars and named a herdsman's son as the next dynasty. Ardeshir built the Sasanian empire on that prophecy and his own ferocity. To face this gate you must understand how empires begin.
